Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that very high serum CA 19-9 levels may not necessarily be a contraindication to pancreaticoduodenectomy (also known as the Whipple procedure). According to one of the completed answers, patients who normalized their CA 19-9 levels postoperatively had equivalent survival to those with normal preoperative CA 19-9 levels. Additionally, another answer states that preoperative serum CA 19-9 level by itself should not preclude surgery in carefully staged patients.

It is essential to note that the severity of elevated CA 19-9 levels can vary widely among individuals and may be influenced by various factors such as the underlying cause of elevation, overall health, and other medical conditions. A thorough evaluation and staging are crucial before making a decision regarding pancreaticoduodenectomy.

In summary, while very high serum CA 19-9 levels might be associated with an increased risk of complications after surgery, it is not necessarily a contraindication to the procedure alone. Patients should be carefully evaluated and staged to determine the best course of treatment.
